Getting started with a5px

Source: vignettes/a5px.Rmd
a5px.Rmd

a5px turns raster pixels into statistics over A5 cells, the equal-area pentagons of a discrete global grid. It reads GeoTIFF and Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF (COG) files from disk or a cloud store, assigns each pixel to a cell, and returns one row per cell. This article walks through the readers and their options. The examples run on small rasters shipped with the package; those that need the network are shown but not run.

library(a5px)

Reading a raster

a5_raster_info() describes a file without reading its pixels: size, data type, block grid, overviews, CRS and its envelope in WGS 84.

cog <- system.file("extdata", "overview_cog.tif", package = "a5px")
info <- a5_raster_info(cog)
info[c("width", "height", "dtype", "crs", "block", "bbox")]
#> $width
#> [1] 512
#> 
#> $height
#> [1] 512
#> 
#> $dtype
#> [1] "float32"
#> 
#> $crs
#> [1] "EPSG:32633"
#> 
#> $block
#> [1] 256 256
#> 
#> $bbox
#> [1] 13.72488 45.14639 13.92331 45.28664

a5_read_raster() aggregates it into cells at one A5 resolution. Each row is a cell, keyed by an a5R::a5_cell, with one column per band:

cells <- a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L)
cells
#> # A tibble: 516 × 2
#>    cell             band_01
#>    <a5_cell>          <dbl>
#>  1 514456a600000000    138.
#>  2 514456aa00000000    137.
#>  3 514456ae00000000    138.
#>  4 514456b200000000    139.
#>  5 514473c600000000    139.
#>  6 514473e600000000    140.
#>  7 514473ea00000000    140.
#>  8 514473ee00000000    139.
#>  9 514473f200000000    138.
#> 10 514473f600000000    139.
#> # ℹ 506 more rows

a5view draws the cells as a ggplot2 layer, geom_a5(), which takes the cell column as its cell aesthetic:

library(ggplot2)
library(a5view)

ggplot(cells, aes(cell = cell, fill = band_01)) +
  geom_a5(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_void()

The resolution sets the cell size. a5R::a5_cell_area() gives the area in square metres: a resolution-13 cell, about 0.5 km^2, holds some 560 of this raster’s 30 m pixels.

a5R::a5_cell_area(c(10L, 13L, 16L, 18L))
#> Units: [m^2]
#> [1] 3.242910e+07 5.067047e+05 7.917261e+03 4.948288e+02

Resolutions run from 0 to 29. Resolution 30 is refused for now: the a5 crate returns resolution-29 cells for some points at 30.

Three outputs

The three readers share one engine and differ in what they return:

  • a5_read_raster() returns a tibble, one numeric column per band and statistic.
  • a5_read_raster_arrow() returns an Arrow table, with the same columns or, with as_vector = TRUE, one list column per statistic holding every band.
  • a5_raster_to_parquet() writes a Parquet file straight from Rust, which avoids holding the result in R.
tab <- a5_read_raster_arrow(cog, resolution = 13L)
tab
#> Table
#> 516 rows x 2 columns
#> $cell <uint64>
#> $band_01 <double>
#> 
#> See $metadata for additional Schema metadata

pq <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
a5_raster_to_parquet(cog, pq, resolution = 13L, compression = "zstd")
arrow::read_parquet(pq, as_data_frame = FALSE)
#> Table
#> 516 rows x 2 columns
#> $cell <uint64 not null>
#> $band_01 <double not null>
#> 
#> See $metadata for additional Schema metadata

a5px_write_parquet() writes a tibble or Arrow table from the first two. The Arrow and Parquet outputs record the read’s provenance in their metadata: the A5 index version, the a5 crate and a5px versions, the sampling mode, the decode, whether overviews were allowed and any nodata override.

Statistics

stat takes one or more of "mean", "sum", "count", "min", "max", "var", "sd", "majority" and "fractions", all computed in one pass. "npix" adds the number of pixels in each cell with any valid band.

a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L, stat = c("mean", "sd", "count", "npix"))
#> # A tibble: 524 × 5
#>    cell             band_01_mean band_01_sd band_01_count  npix
#>    <a5_cell>               <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 514456a600000000         138.      0.225           113   113
#>  2 514456aa00000000         137.      0.454           560   560
#>  3 514456ae00000000         138.      0.307           313   313
#>  4 514456b200000000         139.      0.224           112   112
#>  5 514473c600000000         139.      0.466           438   438
#>  6 514473e600000000         140.      0.219           110   110
#>  7 514473ea00000000         140.      0.292           283   283
#>  8 514473ee00000000         139.      0.454           564   564
#>  9 514473f200000000         138.      0.502           560   560
#> 10 514473f600000000         139.      0.306           312   312
#> # ℹ 514 more rows

sum and count let partial results be merged without re-reading the raster, as in chunked reads.

For integer class labels such as land cover, "majority" gives each cell’s most common class and "fractions" the share of each class, as a list column:

a5_read_raster(landcover, resolution = 12L, stat = c("majority", "fractions"))

Pixels equal to the file’s nodata value, and NaN pixels, are missing: they enter no statistic. src_nodata overrides the file’s value.

Sampling modes

mode controls how pixels map to cells.

  • "forward" (the default) assigns each pixel to the cell that contains its centre. It suits cells several pixels across.
  • "overlay" splits each pixel between the cells it overlaps, in proportion to area, estimated by supersampling the pixel (subsamples). Means become area-weighted and sum conserves totals, such as population counts. Only pixels on a cell boundary pay for the supersampling.
  • "centroid" samples the raster at each cell’s centre, for cells smaller than pixels. interp picks the kernel: "nearest" (the default), "bilinear", "bicubic" or "lanczos".
a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 11L, mode = "overlay", stat = c("mean", "sum"))
#> # A tibble: 44 × 3
#>    cell             band_01_mean band_01_sum
#>    <a5_cell>               <dbl>       <dbl>
#>  1 514456a000000000         137.     206570.
#>  2 514473a000000000         141.       1690.
#>  3 514473e000000000         138.     646628.
#>  4 5144742000000000         136.     438124.
#>  5 514474e000000000         131.     184203.
#>  6 5145082000000000         107.     755635.
#>  7 5145086000000000         111.     991566.
#>  8 514508a000000000         116.    1046736.
#>  9 514508e000000000         111.     790444.
#> 10 5145092000000000         111.     115632.
#> # ℹ 34 more rows
a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 18L, mode = "centroid", interp = "bilinear",
               bbox = c(13.80, 45.20, 13.81, 45.21))
#> # A tibble: 1,766 × 2
#>    cell             band_01
#>    <a5_cell>          <dbl>
#>  1 5145089800800000    119.
#>  2 5145089802800000    118.
#>  3 5145089803800000    118.
#>  4 5145089806800000    118.
#>  5 5145089808800000    118.
#>  6 5145089809800000    118.
#>  7 514508980a800000    118.
#>  8 514508980b800000    118.
#>  9 514508980c800000    118.
#> 10 514508980d800000    118.
#> # ℹ 1,756 more rows

Under "overlay", majority and fractions are area-weighted too.

Overviews

With stat = "mean" in forward or overlay mode, a5px reads the coarsest COG overview that still has several pixels per cell, which cuts the download for coarse resolutions. Other statistics, such as sum, count or max, always read full-resolution pixels, since an overview changes them. use_overviews = FALSE turns this off.

Subsets

Bounding box

bbox reads only the pixels inside a WGS 84 box, c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax). A box with xmin > xmax crosses the antimeridian.

b <- info$bbox
west <- c(b[1], b[2], (b[1] + b[3]) / 2, b[4])
a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L, bbox = west)
#> # A tibble: 270 × 2
#>    cell             band_01
#>    <a5_cell>          <dbl>
#>  1 5145080200000000    104.
#>  2 5145080600000000    105.
#>  3 5145080a00000000    106.
#>  4 5145080e00000000    105.
#>  5 5145081200000000    106.
#>  6 5145081600000000    107.
#>  7 5145081a00000000    107.
#>  8 5145081e00000000    108.
#>  9 5145082200000000    109.
#> 10 5145082600000000    110.
#> # ℹ 260 more rows

Areas of interest

aoi keeps the A5 cells of a polygon, selected as by a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells(): containment = "centre" keeps the cells whose centre is inside, "overlapping" every cell the polygon touches. Selection is by cell, so an included cell gets all its valid pixels, including any outside the polygon. aoi takes what a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells() does: sf or sfc objects, wk geometries, WKT, a terra SpatVector or a lon/lat matrix.

aoi <- wk::rct(13.80, 45.18, 13.86, 45.24, crs = wk::wk_crs_longlat())
a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L, aoi = aoi, containment = "overlapping")
#> # A tibble: 81 × 2
#>    cell             band_01
#>    <a5_cell>          <dbl>
#>  1 5145088e00000000    116.
#>  2 5145089200000000    117.
#>  3 5145089600000000    119.
#>  4 5145089a00000000    117.
#>  5 51450e6e00000000    121.
#>  6 51450e8200000000    123.
#>  7 51450e8600000000    122.
#>  8 51450e8a00000000    121.
#>  9 51450e8e00000000    122.
#> 10 51450e9200000000    121.
#> # ℹ 71 more rows

The two rules side by side, with the AOI outlined. "overlapping" adds the cells the edge cuts, and each keeps its pixels outside the polygon:

by_rule <- lapply(c("centre", "overlapping"), function(rule) {
  out <- a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L, aoi = aoi, containment = rule)
  out$containment <- rule
  out
})
ggplot(vctrs::vec_rbind(!!!by_rule)) +
  geom_a5(aes(cell = cell, fill = band_01), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = sf::st_as_sf(aoi), fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~containment) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_void()

In centroid mode the AOI’s cells are sampled directly, so the polygon is covered without gaps.

Chunked reads

A read holds every cell it touches in memory until it finishes, so very large reads are best split by bbox. bbox_align = "block" takes the COG blocks whose origin lies in each box, so a set of boxes that tiles the raster fetches every block once, and sum and count add up exactly across chunks:

east <- c((b[1] + b[3]) / 2, b[2], b[3], b[4])
parts <- lapply(list(west, east), function(bb) {
  a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L, bbox = bb, bbox_align = "block",
                 stat = c("sum", "count"), use_overviews = FALSE)
})
whole <- a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 13L, stat = c("sum", "count"),
                        use_overviews = FALSE)
c(chunked = sum(sapply(parts, function(p) sum(p[[3]]))), whole = sum(whole[[3]]))
#> chunked   whole 
#>  262144  262144

Remote chunks reuse the header and blocks they share through a session cache (see Remote sources).

Several files

src takes several files, read in one pass. How they combine depends on what they hold:

# bands stored one file each: one column per file, named by names(src)
a5_read_raster(c(red = red_url, nir = nir_url), 14L, separate = TRUE)

# adjacent tiles, or repeat captures, of one product: pixels pooled
a5_read_raster(c(tile_a, tile_b), 14L)

# a statistic per capture, then reduced across captures in each cell
a5_read_raster(captures, 14L, composite = "median")
a5_read_raster(captures, 14L, composite = "count") # captures per cell

Pooled files must have the same bands and pixel size. Every valid pixel enters its cell once, so cells on a seam between tiles combine exactly, and where files overlap every capture counts. composite computes stat for each file and reduces across files, weighting each by its valid pixels in the cell. Single-band files without band descriptions look alike to the pooling check, so set separate = TRUE for files that hold different bands.

Decoding stored values

scoff = TRUE applies the scale and offset each band declares, turning stored integers into physical units:

sc <- system.file("extdata", "scoff_int16.tif", package = "a5px")
a5_raster_info(sc)[c("scale", "offset")]
#> $scale
#> [1] 0.01 0.50
#> 
#> $offset
#> [1]  0 10
a5_read_raster(sc, resolution = 12L, scoff = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 136 × 3
#>    cell              rh98 band_02
#>    <a5_cell>        <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1 514eaab800000000  5.00  -231. 
#>  2 514eaac800000000  4.26  -194. 
#>  3 514eaaf800000000  3.50  -157. 
#>  4 514eab0800000000  2.75  -118. 
#>  5 514eab3800000000  1.99   -80.7
#>  6 514eabe800000000  1.24   -43  
#>  7 6ab3f20800000000  4.97   495  
#>  8 6ab3f21800000000  5.38   489. 
#>  9 6ab3f23800000000  5.63   462. 
#> 10 6ab3f24800000000  6.13   452. 
#> # ℹ 126 more rows

A linear decode gives the same result before or after averaging. A quantized code does not: the mean of codes is not the code of the mean. dequant decodes each pixel before it enters the statistics. It takes any vectorised R function of the integer codes; a5px evaluates it once per possible code and passes the table to Rust, so the source must be an integer type of 16 bits or fewer. dequant_aef decodes Alpha Earth Foundations embeddings, sign(x) * (x / 127.5)^2:

aef <- system.file("extdata", "aef_int8.tif", package = "a5px")
a5_read_raster(aef, resolution = 13L, dequant = dequant_aef)
#> # A tibble: 194 × 3
#>    cell                  A01      A02
#>    <a5_cell>           <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 5160d62a00000000 -0.632   -0.134  
#>  2 5160d62e00000000 -0.308   -0.190  
#>  3 5160d63200000000 -0.300   -0.0190 
#>  4 5160d63600000000 -0.0223   0.0934 
#>  5 5160d68200000000  0.0554   0.272  
#>  6 5160d68600000000  0.0655  -0.249  
#>  7 5160d68a00000000  0.207   -0.142  
#>  8 5160d68e00000000 -0.00866 -0.359  
#>  9 5160d69200000000 -0.0793   0.303  
#> 10 5160d69600000000 -0.549    0.00855
#> # ℹ 184 more rows

A function that returns NA for some codes marks those pixels missing. Setting dequant also turns use_overviews off, since overviews built by averaging codes decode wrongly.

Coarser resolutions

a5_aggregate() summarises a result at a coarser resolution without re-reading the raster. Each cell goes to the coarse cell containing its centre, and means are weighted by each cell’s pixel count:

fine <- a5_read_raster(cog, resolution = 14L, stat = c("mean", "npix"))
coarse <- a5_aggregate(fine, resolution = 11L)
coarse
#> # A tibble: 44 × 3
#>    cell             band_01  npix
#>    <a5_cell>          <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 514456a000000000    137.  1282
#>  2 514473a000000000    141.    39
#>  3 514473e000000000    138.  4909
#>  4 5144742000000000    136.  3264
#>  5 514474e000000000    131.  1391
#>  6 5145082000000000    107.  7260
#>  7 5145086000000000    111.  8694
#>  8 514508a000000000    116.  8717
#>  9 514508e000000000    111.  7279
#> 10 5145092000000000    111.  1130
#> # ℹ 34 more rows

Coarse cells along the raster’s edge extend past it, and their means cover only the part with pixels:

both <- vctrs::vec_rbind(
  tibble::tibble(cell = fine$cell, band_01 = fine$band_01, res = "resolution 14"),
  tibble::tibble(cell = coarse$cell, band_01 = coarse$band_01, res = "resolution 11")
)
both$res <- factor(both$res, levels = c("resolution 14", "resolution 11"))
ggplot(both, aes(cell = cell, fill = band_01)) +
  geom_a5() +
  facet_wrap(~res) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_void()

Remote sources

src may be an s3://, gs://, az:// or http(s):// URL, or a GDAL /vsis3/, /vsigs/, /vsiaz/ or /vsicurl/ path. Reads fetch byte ranges and never download the whole file. Cloud clients are configured from the environment first, every AWS_*, GOOGLE_* and AZURE_* variable that object_store understands plus GDAL’s AWS_NO_SIGN_REQUEST, and from store_opts second, so an explicit option wins.

url <- "s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/tge-labs/aef/v1/annual/2020/22S/tile.tiff"

# a public bucket outside us-east-1
a5_read_raster(url, 14L, store_opts = c(aws_region = "us-west-2",
                                        aws_skip_signature = "true"))

# check region, endpoint and signing before a long read
a5px_store_config(url, store_opts = c(aws_region = "us-west-2"))

An S3 source with no credentials configured is read unsigned where no instance metadata service answers, which reads public data. The shared credentials file and AWS_PROFILE are not read. See ?a5px for each provider’s settings.

Remote reads keep the byte ranges they fetch in a session cache, so a read split into chunks, or repeated, fetches each block once. a5px_set_cache() sets its budget (an eighth of a container memory limit, or 512 MiB without one, by default), a5px_cache_info() reports its size and the requests made, and a5px_clear_cache() empties it.

Performance

  • Workers and requests. cpu_workers sets the threads that decode and index pixels; it defaults to the CPUs available to R, which respects container limits. io_concurrency sets the remote requests a read keeps in flight, 32 by default. a5px_concurrency() sets both for the session, or for one expression with with().
  • Bands. For COGs that store each band separately (INTERLEAVE=BAND), as embedding rasters often do, bands limits the download to the bands selected: reading 8 of 64 bands of a 2.8 GB AEF tile takes 24 s instead of 62 s. bands takes 1-based indices or band names.
  • Memory. The cells of a read are held until it finishes: the mean of 64 bands over a 2048 x 2048 AEF window, 848,000 cells at resolution 18, peaks at about 1.1 GB. For larger areas, chunk by bbox. value_type = "float32" halves the size of Arrow and Parquet output.
  • Profiling. Sys.setenv(A5PX_PROFILE = "1") prints the time spent in each stage of a read.
a5_raster_to_parquet(
  url, "embeddings.parquet",
  resolution = 14L, bands = 1:8, dequant = dequant_aef,
  value_type = "float32", compression = "zstd"
)

Supported rasters

  • Formats. Tiled GeoTIFF and COG with ZSTD, Deflate, LZW, JPEG, PackBits or no compression; internal mask bands are applied. Strip-based GeoTIFFs fail with a clear error.
  • CRSs. EPSG codes, WKT in a citation field, or the GeoKey parameters, which covers custom projections written by GDAL without an EPSG code, such as a centred Lambert azimuthal equal-area. Rasters crossing the antimeridian, and pixel-is-point rasters, are handled.
  • NoData. The dataset-wide GDAL nodata value, and NaN. GeoTIFF has no per-band nodata.
